react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome is dominated by arachidonic acid (AA) and its eicosanoid derivatives, producing a near-perfect cross-paradigm signal. In the RaMP ORA (merged Reactome + SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways), the top-scoring pathway is Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) with a fold enrichment of 1,251 and FDR = 3.16 × 10⁻¹³, driven by five of the eight input metabolites: 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-prostaglandin J2 (15d-PGJ2), arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, and leukotriene A4 (LTA4). The same five metabolites reproduce this hit across fourteen nearly-identical SMPDB drug-action pathways (NSAID-related), all sharing FDR = 8.28 × 10⁻¹³. The Mummichog m/z-direct analysis confirms Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) as the top-ranked network (p = 0.00286), with 11 of 11 input compounds resolving to the AA network — a 100% overlap within that network. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently returns KEGG:hsa00590 (Arachidonic acid metabolism) as the top hit, with four of four successfully mapped metabolites (arachidonic acid, LTA4, 15-HETE, 5-HETE). Glycerophospholipid metabolism (MUMM rank 2, p = 0.00714) and Leukotriene metabolism (MUMM rank 4, p = 0.033) are secondary network sub-themes. Arachidonic acid (C00219, CHEBI:15843) is the metabolic hub: it is the substrate for COX-derived 15d-PGJ2, LOX-derived HETEs (5-HETE, 15-HETE), and 5-LOX-derived LTA4. Acetylcysteine, fructose 1-phosphate, and dopamine appear only in secondary or non-significant pathways and are not driver metabolites of the primary eicosanoid signal.
